explain.say: If you met someone speaking English from 1,200 years ago, you would hardly understand a word! English has changed hugely. Look at the timeline on the board. It starts around 450 CE, when Angles and Saxons sailed to Britain. Their language is called Old English.

faq.a: Old English is the language of the Anglo-Saxons, spoken from about 450 to 1100 CE. It looks like a foreign language today. The poem Beowulf is written in it.

After the Norman Conquest in 1066, French was the language of rulers for about 300 years. Thousands of French words entered English, especially for law, food and government, like court, beef and parliament.
Estimates say about 1.5 billion people speak English, but only around 400 million as a first language. Most speakers learned it as a second language.
asks: How many English speakers are there?

faq.q: Why do we have words like cow and beef for the same animal?
faq.a: After 1066, English-speaking farmers raised cows, from Old English, while French-speaking nobles ate beef, from French boeuf. Both words stayed.

faq.q: What did the Vikings give English?
faq.a: Norse gave English everyday words like sky, egg, knife, window and the pronouns they, them and their.

facts: The pronouns they, them and their came into English from Old Norse.
William Caxton set up the first printing press in England, at Westminster, in 1476.
Samuel Johnson's Dictionary of the English Language was published in 1755.
